Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of STUDYID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: As defined per protocol. Required when study has more than 1 part ( e.g., part A, dose escalation and part B, dose evaluation). In SDTM it is mapped in STUDYID by some sponsor companies.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of subject type.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique character representation of SUBJTYP. For first-in-human studies, the value can be "Healthy volunteers".

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of USUBJID.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of SUBJID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Must be identical to the ADSL variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of SITEID. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived sequence for the whole dataset. Sequential values should start with 1 on the first non-header row of the data file (i.e., skipping the variable names) and incrementing by 1 for each subsequent row. These are basically row numbers. It is often used for convenience purposes and merging of PK and PD datasets. It can also be useful for the tracking of outlier exclusion, since the variable is preserved from the original to the final dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Actual Rel Time from First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: Actual elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to study treatment. Could be negative. Derived from (ADTM of the current event/record of the subject) - (ADTM of the first dosing event/record of the subject).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Units for all reference times AFRLT, APRLT, NFRLT, NPRLT. Add the unit here or in the time variable label.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Actual Rel Time from Previous Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived from (ADTM of the current event/record of the subject) - (ADTM of the previous dosing event/record of the subject).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Nominal Rel Time from First Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: Planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from first exposure to study treatment. For PK it will be in the PC dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Nominal Rel Time from Previous Dose
Variables.CDISC Notes: For PK it can be derived from "planned elapsed time (for sample point or start of sampling interval) from reference exposure to study treatment" or equivalent variable that has nominal time in the PC dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Occasion is a grouping variable. It groups dose and concentration observations for a particular dosing. The implementation is taken directly from the specs/protocol and defined by the modeler. This is a popPK software variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: It can be captured prior to the modeling or after some analysis, with possible iterations and adjustments. Some possible reasons: BLOQ, biological implausibility, IWER > threshold, incorrect dosing information. There can be several reasons for flagging data during the dataset creation (e.g., day 1 pre-dose samples, missing sample information, deviation of actual time from nominal time > threshold).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: It can be captured prior to the modeling or after some analysis, with possible iterations and adjustments. Some possible reasons: BLOQ, biological implausibility, outlier based on variability metrics, incorrect dosing information, day 1 pre-dose sample. This can also be coded through numbers that are connected with different reasons. Based on data specification. Could come from multiple sources (e.g., SDTM or ADaM source, CRITyFN variable). Examples of exclusions can be found in Section 3.4, Standard Flags and Record Identifiers in Population PK Dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Captures primary reason for identifying the record for data issues (e.g., dose time imputation flags). A sequential number starting with 1 and increments with each unique reason. Examples of reasons for identification of data issue can be found in Section 3.4, Standard Flags and Record Identifiers in Population PK Dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Character version of FLGREAS.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: EVID=1 is Dosing Event, EVID=0 is observation. \n It can be expanded to other numbers as defined in the dataset specs. This is a popPK software variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Analyte/drug name/other measurements (e.g., PC.PCTEST for PK, EX or ADEX for dose, ADLB for labs).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of DVID. Convention is normally 0=dose, 1=for the first observation of interest, etc. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived based on the specifications from modeler. This is a popPK software variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric result of dependent variable applicable to observation events. DV is a widely used notation in the field of pharmacometrics since its inception for the value of dependent variable (observation). This is a copy of AVAL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric analysis value described by PARAM.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unit for DV and AVAL

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Result or Finding in Standard Format
Variables.CDISC Notes: Character results/findings of dependent variable in a standard format. The purpose of this column is to capture which records are BLQ or ALQ in the DV column; for example, PC.PCSTRESC (SDTM), AVAL (ADaM). U is a replacement for the dataset name from where the value came from (e.g., USTRESC is equal to PCSTRESC for PC records).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: If DV= . then MDV=1. \n (When DV is missing for observation then MDV=1, when EVID=1 then MDV=1) \n This is a popPK software variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: In assay report

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: LLOQ of PK, PD and any other sources

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Below Lower Limit of Quant Flag
Variables.CDISC Notes: N, Y. Set to Y when the analysis value is below the limit of quantification.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Below Lower Limit of Quant Flag (N)
Variables.CDISC Notes: 0=N, 1=Y. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Above the Upper Limit of Quant Flag
Variables.CDISC Notes: N, Y. Set to Y when the analysis value is above the limit of quantification.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Above the Upper Limit of Quant Flag (N)
Variables.CDISC Notes: 0=N, 1=Y. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Only populated on dosing records

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: DOSEA represents the actual treatment dosage associated with the record. Could be amount (mg) or weight based dose (mg/kg). Units of AMT and DOSEA can be same or different. \n This is the actual numeric amount of the dose used for the population analysis and may differ from the EX.EXDOSE. It can be derived from the EX.EXDOSE or based on related dose. Populated on all individual records as carry-forward.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Total Daily Amt of Dose Received (unit)
Variables.CDISC Notes: Used mostly for BID dosing schemes

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Duration associated with infusion (IV, SC); distinct from TRTDURD, TRTDURM, and TRTDURY, which reference the duration of the entire study rather than the duration of a single treatment event. "EX dataset". \n Derived from EXENDTC - EXSTDTC \n The label should contain the unit of time. Usually same unit as time variables.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Calculated as the amount of dose received divided by the dose duration. Certain modeling methods may require that RATE is set to a specific value. \n The label should contain the unit (e.g., mg/hr).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Describes the dosing frequency for multiple doses (e.g., 24 for QD, 12 for BID, if time unit is hours).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Number of additional doses like the current dosing event until the next captured dose (e.g., if the value is 1 then 1 additional dose; if value is 2 then 2 additional doses). It is commonly used for long-lasting studies with frequent dosing in order to not have the dataset extremely large.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: A steady-state dose is a dose that is presumed to be the last of a series of implied doses, each exactly like the dose in question, given at a regular interval specified by the II data item and leading to steady state by the time the steady-state dose is given.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Type of formulation (e.g., tablet, capsule, aerosol); EX.EXDOSFRM or protocol

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Unique numerical representation of FORM. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from the corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Route of treatment delivery. May be derived from EX.EXROUTE.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived from ROUTE as one-on-one unique match. The numeric versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding character pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Record-level identifier that reflects cycle and may be of particular importance for studies that examine concentrations in cancer patients from AVISIT or protocol.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Derived from ACYCLE as one-on-one unique match. The character versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding numeric pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Subject-level variable. Could be some sort of subpopulation.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Character representation of the COHORT variable. There must be a one-to-one mapping to COHORT. The character versions of the primary/character variables can be assigned from its corresponding numeric pair variable.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.Variable Label: Date and Time of the Event
Variables.CDISC Notes: Datetime associated with event ID represented in ISO 8601 character format. U is a replacement for the dataset name from where the value came from (e.g., UDTC is equal to PCDTC for PC records).

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Variable may be derived from VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets. Weight is associated with sampling time. SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Variable may be derived from VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets. Weight is associated with the last assessment prior to dosing. Use flags for baseline. SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset. If the definition of this variable in the modeling plan is the same as in the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Variable may be derived from baseline VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets. SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset. If the definition of this variable in the modeling plan is the same as in the statistical analysis plan (SAP), then use the variable in ADSL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Variable may be derived from baseline VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets (SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset) or derived. ADSL.BMIBL for baseline and VS.BMI for time-varying or derived. If the definition of this variable in the modeling plan is the same as in the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Variable may be derived from baseline VS.VSTEST and VS.VSSTRESN but may also be pulled in from other datasets (SDTM.VS or a Vital Signs analysis dataset) or derived. ADSL.BSABL for baseline and VS.BSA for time-varying or derived. If the definition of this variable in the modeling plan is the same as in the SAP then use the variable in ADSL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: DM.AGE or ADSL.AGE. If analysis needs require a derived age that does not match ADSL.AGE, then AAGE (Analysis Age) must be added.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Number of years between BRTHDT and ADT

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: The sex of the subject is a required variable in ADSL; must be identical to ADSL.SEX.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of SEX. Can be extended to other values beyond 1 and 2. \n Example values can be as follows: \n 1=M, 2=F

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: The race of the subject is a required variable in ADSL; identical to ADSL.RACE. May categorize differently if analysis demands.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of RACE, e.g., codes used as per the specification. \n 1=American Indian or Alaska Native, 2=Asian, 3=Black/African American, 4=Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, 5=White \n If races need to be categorized differently, then use variables ARACE and ARACEN.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: To be able to allow different definitions of race. For example, allowing to code American Indian/Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander are coded as "Other". This is analysis-specific and could vary based on analysis needs.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of ARACE; for example: \n 1=White, 2=Black/African American, 3=Asian, 4=Other, 5=Unknown (e.g., not reported). American Indian/Alaska Native and Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander are coded as 4.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Ethnicity as needed for analysis. May be derived.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of AETHNIC.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: REGIONy is a permissible variable in ADSL.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of REGIONy.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: DM.COUNTRY or ADSL.COUNTRY

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: COUNTRYL is a human-readable name of the DM.COUNTRY value.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Numeric version of COUNTRY.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Use the baseline lab value for creatinine serum per the algorithm defined in the SAP.

Variables.CDISC Notes: Use the baseline lab value for creatinine clearance per the algorithm defined in the SAP. A formula may be suggested if the value does not exist in the lab dataset.

Variables.CDISC Notes: Use the baseline lab value for eGFR per the algorithm defined in the SAP. A formula may be suggested if the value does not exist in the lab dataset.

Variables.Data Structure Name: Basic Data Structure Population Pharmacokinetic Analysis
Variables.CDISC Notes: Use the baseline lab value for aspartate transaminase per the algorithm defined in the SAP.
